initial:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset: a coherent 16-frame south-facing locomotion sprite sheet for the existing hooded player in an elevated top-down urban action game. Reference image is the character identity and exact viewpoint, not a side-scroller. Preserve charcoal hood and coat, concealed face, brown diagonal strap and belt pouches, gloves, knee pads and boots. Preserve the asymmetrical strap on the same anatomical side. Restrained urban street-theater costume, not fantasy wizard or armored soldier. No new equipment.
Create exactly 16 distinct sequential movement poses in a precise 4 columns by 4 rows square grid, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. All 16 sprites face toward screen bottom from the SAME elevated camera angle, showing top of hood and shoulders. No turning, no profile views. No labels, grid lines, text or cast shadows. Transparent background.
Each equal cell contains full character with generous transparent margins, identical scale and body proportions. Hip/root center remains at same location within each cell; consistent ground reference. Animate a brisk grounded walk cycle in place with clearly changing leg and opposed arm positions, natural boot contacts, passing poses and small vertical body motion. Frame1 left foot forward contact/right foot back; 2-4 left support and right recovery; 5 right passing under hips; 6-8 right reaching forward; 9 right foot forward contact/left foot back;10-12 right support and left recovery;13 left passing;14-16 left reaching to next frame1. No repeated neutral poses, no decorative jitter pretending to be animation. Frame16 flows into frame1 without duplicating it. Exactly two legs, two arms, feet always identifiable. Coat tails follow motion without concealing the feet. Maintain identical hood volume, shoulder width, material palette, line weight and upper-left lighting across cells. Carefully drawn detailed hand-painted sprite finish matching reference. This is one continuous gait, not sixteen redesigns.
correction:
Edit the supplied 4x4 hooded-player animation sheet. Keep the exact character design, elevated top-down south-facing viewpoint, clothing details, scale, lighting, transparent background, grid and 16 cells. Correct ONLY the locomotion phase sequence to be temporally coherent. Previous result switches leading legs repeatedly too soon. We need one complete two-step walk over all16cells read rowmajor, not16 random walking poses.
Screen-left and screen-right refer to the viewer's image.
Frame1 screen-left boot forward/down, screen-right boot back/up.
Frame2 same left support, right heel lifting.
Frame3 left leg supports, right knee recovers toward body.
Frame4 right knee advancing, right boot still behind left boot.
Frame5 passing: right boot under hips beside left leg, left boot now travels rearward.
Frame6 right boot reaches a little forward.
Frame7 right boot reaches farther forward, left heel lifting.
Frame8 right boot nearly full forward extension.
Frame9 right boot full forward/down contact, left boot full back/up.
Frame10 same right support, left heel lifting.
Frame11 right leg supports, left knee recovers toward body.
Frame12 left knee advancing, left boot still behind right boot.
Frame13 passing: left boot under hips beside right leg, right boot travels rearward.
Frame14 left boot reaches a little forward.
Frame15 left boot reaches farther forward, right heel lifting.
Frame16 left boot nearly full forward extension, smoothly leading to frame1.
Arms move opposite legs smoothly through the16frames. Small natural vertical hip motion, no skating, no leg crossing, no duplicate idle poses. Torso stays square south toward bottom of screen, hood volume and chest straps stable. Ground projection and each sprite's hip-root center fixed across cells. Keep all boots visible and entirely within their cells. NO text numbers lines or floor.
